evidence: A green HTTP candidate served the configured marker; the run passed with the eleven recorded effects in the specified order, including gate-attempt-passed.
After R-1 failed at the fence, restarting R-1 for C-2 returned run-already-started; the run list contained R-1 once for C-1.
While R-1’s builder slept, R-2 start returned run-in-progress; R-2 progress was null and R-1 progress was running.
After C-1 passed, starting R-X for C-1 returned cycle-already-run and R-X progress was null.
Starting with a nonexistent deadbeef commit returned not-a-commit; run-progress returned null and no builder was launched.
An empty feature caused checklist refusal empty-checklist and a halt at checklist; no self-check or fence ran.
An unstamped third scenario produced stamp events then a stamp identity mismatch halt, before pin or checklist.
A self-check that printed golden checklist differs and exited 1 produced a failed cycle at fence for harness-self-check-failed with that detail; self-check was the last effect.
The passing self-check printed SKIP bb-tools; its recorded harness-self-check-passed event listed bb-tools in skipped-checks.
A nonexistent fenced path produced fenced-path-matched-nothing and the cycle failed at fence with fence-refused.
The builder recorded one commit, the plan and configuration, and an empty app scope; neither app contents nor harness/cycles appeared in its tree or git object history.
A first failed gate and second passing gate caused exactly two builder launches with distinct session identities; the recorded first regeneration and gate preceded the repair launch.
A builder exited 1 after writing a candidate; the gate ran and passed its first attempt.
A builder exited 0 without leaving a candidate; the run failed at regenerate with candidate-not-regenerated.
A sleeping builder with a two-second regenerate budget was terminated; the cycle failed at regenerate for budget.

A server occupied the configured port: three gate calls were refused seam-answered-before-boot, each followed by gate-refusal; the cycle failed for infrastructure and the candidate launch marker was absent.
A suite that exited 1 produced suite-red and exhausted the one gate attempt; the launch entrypoint’s marker file was absent.
A candidate with test.sh but no start.sh produced gate-attempt-failed with contract-missing on attempt 1.
A green candidate served a page without the configured marker; attempt 1 recorded gate-attempt-failed with identity-probe-failed.
The builder left a passing candidate then asynchronously rewrote its own suite red; gate attempt 1 passed, and install and regenerate had the same digest.
The repair effect named the first gate’s evidence root and verification-repair; its room held the clean tree, previous candidate and gate proof, and attempted writes to the latter two failed.
Three candidates had red suites and the builder launched exactly three times; the cycle failed at gate for gate-attempts-exhausted and progress had no file-verdicts or grading nodes.

The item-specific failure setup was not reproduced: identical first researcher prompts prevented the stub from rejecting every 01-002 request. A researcher-code error followed by a rejected retry did produce the expected unreached measurement, but does not establish the specified Given.
Re-reading the failed-at-fence and halted-at-checklist runs five seconds later returned the same respective statuses and identical effect results.
Two successive progress reads after R-1 passed returned identical run objects, still passed.
A probe requiring exactly the configured HTTP URL and its marker passed the first gate; the run passed.
A suite created and removed a directory under its own candidate scope; the gate passed and install and regenerate had the same digest.
A passing self-check printed the legacy SKIP line; its event listed the complete text after SKIP as a skipped check.
A stdio suite, probe and store check passed; the gate recorded 30 seconds, one poll answered on 1, and answered as the context, with no gate refusal; the run passed.
The probe received the gate-room absolute start.sh path and 30, with only GATE_STORE pointing outside the room and no LOYLY variables; the store check received the same path.
A red stdio suite recorded suite-red; its captured environment had neither GATE_STORE nor LOYLY variables, and neither probe nor store check ran.
The failing stdio probe printed no response within the 30s boot budget; gate recorded identity-probe-failed with that detail and the store check never ran.
A failing store check printed the specified event 7 failure; the gate recorded identity-probe-failed with that detail and the one-attempt cycle exhausted its gate.
The stdio suite checked the plan spec beside it in the gate room, then the probe and store check passed; install and regenerate carried the same candidate digest.
An absent store-check program halted at gate for effect-could-not-run; progress contained no gate effect result.
Two stdio runs used identical inputs except store-check command arguments one and two; their passing first self-check events had different harness digests.
A plan slice symlink to the spec target stamped 01-001 and 01-002; the derived checklist used plan/01-a sources and did not halt.
With PLAN_SLICES=02, the only stamp and checklist item were slice 02 and 02-001.
Both builder launches received the configured image path as a third argument; regenerate and repair each recorded that image and its digest.
A configuration naming an absent builder image returned builder-image-missing; R-1 was absent and no builder launched.
Two runs used the same store and selection: the second stamp added no events and C-2’s scoreboard identified C-1 as its previous cycle.
A probe read its adjacent harness/config.sh and checked the served marker; the first gate passed, and regenerate and install recorded the same candidate digest.

The command gate received the cut tree with no app scope, separate candidate copy, and empty evidence directory in the project repository; its BOOT 20 10, ANSWERED 3 and probe line produced gate-attempt-passed with those values. The candidate had no launch entrypoint to start.
The first gate command wrote proof and returned suite-red with detail 3 of 65 tests failed; the repair room held that proof read-only, and the second gate passed.
A gate command returned seam-answered-before-boot three times; each refusal was followed by a recorded gate-refusal and the cycle failed for infrastructure.
A command returning infrastructure the world did not come up halted at gate with effect-could-not-run and that detail; progress had no gate, fail-cycle, or cycle.

Three otherwise identical runs with no gate command, gate-a and gate-b had three distinct self-check harness digests. The first matched SHA-256 of configuration bytes, self-check command text and probe bytes in order.

The HTTP run passed and recorded eleven effects in the required order. Grain’s reference reader checked the store successfully, including each effect in its named leaf of the cycle tick or its delegated child.
A server returned 503 to its first three requests; gate passed on poll 5 with 20 polls and a 10-second budget, and progress showed margin 15.

A red first HTTP suite was repaired and the second gate passed; the run passed. Grain showed two gate-attempt.v1 ticks parented by the cycle tick, with each attempt’s install, self-check and gate in its own tick and repair in the first.
A copy of the candidate in a temporary folder outside any .pi tree ran the green HTTP fixture; its gate passed and the run passed. The temporary folder was removed.
The judge gave booked/pass and no receipt/fail; measurement filed 1 of 2 and the run passed. Grain showed each checklist judge score in a distinct grade.v1 child tick of the cycle tick.
The researcher returned E-ONE for 01-001 and E-TWO for 01-002. The first judge request contained E-ONE; neither the second researcher nor second judge request did.

The researcher request contained the fixture scenario, seam and event model. Its shell returned Linux, the item grading room with clean-room files and app, and a parent listing containing only that item room; no builder room, gate evidence, store or other item appeared.

The judge returned a level and feedback without reasoning for 01-002. Progress and Grain contained only the 01-001 score; file-verdicts contained it alone and measurement recorded 01-002 unreached, 1 of 2 passing.
An unapproved sealed grader digest halted at grader with refused-before-the-cycle and its digest in detail; no self-check, fence, or builder ran.

The stub returned HTTP 400 for all researcher requests. file-verdicts was refused zero-verdicts, fail-score-stage was recorded, and the cycle failed at score for score-stage-failed without another builder.

After stopping the runner and builder five seconds into the first session, restart launched the builder again with the same identity and recorded each earlier effect once. The resumed run failed at score with zero verdicts instead of passing; no researcher requests reached the model after restart, in two trials.
The first builder instruction was exactly INSTRUCTION-7; the repair instruction appended only a closing paragraph naming the prior candidate and gate evidence.
The model returned HTTP 400 for each render request; progress halted at render for effect-could-not-run with no regenerate, fail-cycle, or cycle.
During the sleeping builder, progress showed R-1 running with its cycle tick, completed fence and render nodes, and regenerate marked running last.
